To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Driscoll andKraay estimator for robust standard errors is well-calibrated and should be used when estimating panel models with cross-sectional dependence, and that the Hausman test is a useful diagnostic tool for fixed-effects regressions that are robust to cross-sectional dependence.

1) the Driscoll and Kray (1998) robust standard errors (SEs) are well calibrated in the presence of cross-sectional dependence; 2) the SEs that are commonly used in the presence of serial correlation, but not cross-sectional dependence, are not well calibrated when there is cross-sectional dependence; and 3) a Hausman-type fixed effect test that is robust to both serial and cross-sectional dependence is presented.
